Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:False. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. evidence.asserts: a slow read is shown as slow - the page never answers with a server-derived value it does not have yet
evidence.checked: PASSES. 149 numeric writes occurred while reads were still pending, and **every one is decorative or client-local, not data**: `stage-hex-num` cycling '01','02','03','04' and `step-dot` numerals - the static stage graphic in the signed-in ops home, which is markup animation rather than a reading. Meanwhile the actual data elements were written ONLY after reads resolved (9 writes after resolve, all `oh-tile-num`: 9, 1, 29, 3 - the real KPI tiles). SO THE DISTINCTION THIS ORACLE NEEDS IS NOT 'were numbers written' BUT 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written' - a page may legitimately render its own static or local figures while waiting. The connectivity badge (`wh-conn-queue`) is the clearest case: it reports the IndexedDB offline-queue depth, a fact the page owns without any read, so a `0` there means 'nothing queued' and is true the moment it is painted. Counting it as a fabrication would have failed a page for being honest about something else. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES A ZERO MEANINGFUL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver on documentElement records every mutation whose resulting text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant. So 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact. THE CONTROL IS NOT OPTIONAL, AND TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS PROBE PROVE WHY. Version 1 tested only the ADDED NODE's own text, so a render that sets innerHTML on a container (numeric leaf nested inside) recorded nothing. Version 2 fixed that and STILL recorded nothing - because addInitScript runs at document start when `document.documentElement` can be null, so `observe()` threw and the observer never attached. Both versions reported **0 writes on pages that visibly populated**, i.e. a flattering zero produced entirely by a broken instrument. Version 3 attaches on a poller AND writes its own numeric sentinel ('4242') that the observer must see; if that control fails the reading is REFUSED rather than reported. All four pages here returned controlOK = true. A ZERO FROM AN UNATTACHED OBSERVER IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN HONEST PAGE - which is the whole reason the control exists.
evidence.value_checked: 149 in-flight numeric writes, all decorative stage numerals; 9 data-tile writes only after resolve; control OK

findings.title: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 2 of its 3 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - pm_assets (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); pm_completions (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 2 of its 3 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - pm_assets (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); pm_completions (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 13 read relation(s), 3 were probed live at the gateway (early_access_emails, pm_assets, pm_completions).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 2 of its 3 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - pm_assets (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); pm_completions (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 13 read relation(s), 3 were probed live at the gateway (early_access_emails, pm_assets, pm_completions).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

scenarios.oracle: the v_alert_truth count on the tile equals the count alert-hub shows for the same hive at the same instant

evidence.asserts: The oracle's literal subject does not exist, and the honest reading is stated rather than forced. ops-home has four KPI tiles - open-jobs, risk-alerts, pm-overdue, low-stock - and NONE of them counts v_alert_truth; 'Risk Alerts' reads v_risk_truth, a different view answering a different question. index touches v_alert_truth in exactly one place: a single banner showing the most recent alert_kind='signature' AND severity='critical' row (LIMIT 1). So there is no alert COUNT here to compare against alert-hub's. What CAN be checked is the oracle's intent - that the two surfaces do not disagree about v_alert_truth for the same hive - and that holds. Both read the same view; index asks for the latest critical, alert-hub lists the 20 most recent signature alerts of any severity with its own documented severity normalisation. On the 2 hives that actually have a critical signature alert, the banner's alert is present in alert-hub's feed (ranked 13th of the 20 shown), so neither surface shows an alert the other denies. A LATENT divergence is recorded rather than glossed: alert-hub caps at 20 while one hive already holds 40 signature alerts, so a critical alert older than 20 more-recent ones would headline index's banner and be absent from alert-hub's feed. That is not the current state in any hive and is noted as a risk, not banked as a defect.
evidence.checked: Checked the premise before testing it - enumerating the actual tiles is what showed the oracle's subject was absent, and testing 'the alert count' without that would have measured the risk tile and called it alert agreement. Verified severity='critical' is REACHABLE before concluding anything from an empty banner: the first hive sampled has 27 signature alerts and 0 critical, which alone looks like a dead filter, but platform-wide 21 rows are critical, so the banner is correctly empty there rather than broken. Agreement was then tested on a hive that HAS one, since a comparison of two empty results proves nothing. One intermediate figure was DISCARDED as wrongly computed: a follow-up query re-ranked rows over the critical-only subset, reporting 'worst rank 1', which is the rank among criticals and not among signature alerts; the retained figure ranks within the full feed, matching the directly observed 13.
evidence.value_checked: ops-home tiles: open-jobs (v_logbook_truth), risk-alerts (v_risk_truth), pm-overdue, low-stock - no v_alert_truth count | index v_alert_truth use: signature+critical banner, LIMIT 1 | alert-hub: alert_kind='signature', all severities, ORDER BY detected_at DESC, alert_id, LIMIT 20 | signature severities present: critical, high | hives with a critical signature alert: 2, banner alert outside alert-hub's top-20 in 0 of them | banner alert observed rank: 13 of 20 | latent: one hive holds 40 signature alerts against a 20-row feed

scenarios.oracle: the composite risk on the landing tile uses the same formula version as analytics - one score, one definition, two surfaces

evidence.asserts: The cross-surface half holds by construction and a REAL version split was found underneath it. index's risk tile counts v_risk_truth WHERE risk_level IN ('critical','high'); analytics reads the same view (its own comment at line 519 says 'same v_risk_truth' and line 840 traces asset_risk_scores -> v_risk_truth). Neither recomputes a score, so the two surfaces cannot hold different formula versions FOR THE SAME ASSET - which is what the oracle literally asks. The defect is one level down and the oracle's phrase 'one score, one definition' is what exposes it: v_risk_truth is DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_name) ORDER BY generated_at DESC, so it keeps the newest row per asset and an asset the scoring batch stops covering keeps its old row indefinitely. Measured: 94 rows on rules-v2, 3 on rules-v1 last scored 2026-07-20 while v2 scores run to 2026-08-19, and BOTH versions appear in the critical/high subset the tile counts. So the two surfaces agree with each other while ranking assets scored by different formulas together. Rather than delete or silently exclude the stale rows - which would UNDERSTATE risk, the worse error on a safety surface - the existing reliability-KPI gate was taught to see it: it already catches a METHODOLOGY fork (cached mtbf_days vs the live engine) and now also reports a VERSION fork, naming the versions, the minority row count, and the fix (re-run batch-risk-scoring for the uncovered assets).
evidence.checked: Confirmed both surfaces read the same view before comparing anything, so the claim rests on a shared source rather than on two numbers happening to match on one hive. Read the view definition rather than assuming a latest-per-asset semantic - the DISTINCT ON is what makes an uncovered asset's stale row persist, and without it the mixed versions would look like ordinary history rather than live data. Checked whether the v1 assets simply had newer v2 rows (450 v2 rows share those asset names) and established they are in OTHER hives, so within their own hive those three genuinely are the newest score. Taught the neighbouring gate instead of writing a new one, and re-ran its --selftest afterwards (PASS) so the addition did not break the check it already performs; the new branch fired on live data rather than only in theory.
evidence.value_checked: v_risk_truth = DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_name) ORDER BY generated_at DESC over asset_risk_scores | model_version: rules-v2=94, rules-v1=3 | both versions present in the critical/high tile subset | rules-v1 rows: AC-02, CP-01, AC-77, all generated 2026-07-20; v2 range 2026-07-20..2026-08-19 | index tile and analytics both read v_risk_truth, neither recomputes | gate now WARNs: '2 model_versions (rules-v1,rules-v2); 3 row(s) not on the majority version' | gate --selftest PASS

evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. ops-home has no PM-compliance percentage, so the oracle's SMRP framing lands on the PM tile it does have, and that tile was missing both halves that make a number checkable. THE UNIT: pm_overdue_count is count(DISTINCT pm_asset_id), so the 28 on screen is ASSETS, while the same view in the same hive returns 69 overdue SCOPE ITEMS. Both are true, they differ by 2.5x, and a label reading only 'PM Overdue' commits to neither, so the reader picks one. THE DENOMINATOR: the hive has 30 PM assets. 28 of 30 is not a backlog, it is a PM programme that has stopped, and on a bare 28 it reads exactly like 28 of 500. scenarios.oracle: the low-stock tile counts by reorder point, not by a hardcoded 'quantity < N'

evidence.asserts: the low-stock tile counts by REORDER POINT, not by a hardcoded quantity threshold
evidence.checked: STATES IT, AND THE TEST DISCRIMINATES. The tile reads "3 LOW STOCK". Against the database for this hive, the two candidate predicates give DIFFERENT answers: `qty_on_hand <= min_qty` (with min_qty > 0) returns 3, while a hardcoded `qty_on_hand < 10` returns 8, out of 27 parts. The tile shows 3, so it is counting each part against ITS OWN reorder point, not a constant. This matters as a NON-VACUITY check, not just a match: if both predicates had returned the same number the agreement would prove nothing, and the row would deserve to stay owed. They differ by 5, so the number on screen can only have come from the reorder-point rule. Corroborated on the other end by inventory.html stockStatus(), which compares `q <= m` where `m = Number(item.min_qty) || 0` - the threshold is read from the row, not from a literal. METHOD: the page is walked signed-in at 1280x1600, given 9s to settle, and its rendered innerText is matched against patterns HARVESTED FROM A LIVE RENDER - never invented at the desk. Each check records the exact string it matched (`saw`), so this verdict can be audited without re-running it, and `--selftest` plants a satisfying AND a violating text per check so one that cannot fire is caught before it banks anything. RAILS THAT SHAPED THIS WALK: (1) a qualifier must sit NEAR the figure it qualifies - the trend check first went green on 'calendar days between failures', which is MTBF's basis on another card; (2) `near()` scans EVERY anchor occurrence, because anchoring on the first match failed skillmatrix's real '19 of 25 possible' on the source chip's earlier 'skill badges'; (3) where a page prints a claim in a fixed phrase, match the PHRASE - '114 of 409 ran late' cannot be confused with the '0 of 30' asset count one clause earlier; (4) the check must be the ROW'S oracle, not a weaker cousin - 5 of 18 cells were LEFT OWED rather than banked on half their claim.

findings.detail: MEASURED, AND THE COUNTS DIFFER BY DESIGN - BUT NOTHING ON EITHER SCREEN SAYS SO. index's tile reads "9 OPEN JOBS"; logbook reads "6 open". Proven against the database, both are individually CORRECT: `select count(*) from logbook where hive_id=<hive> and status='Open'` is 9 (hive-wide, which is what the ops-home dashboard RPC serves), and the same query with `worker_name='Leandro Marquez'` is 6 (logbook's own filter, which is worker-scoped). So this is NOT a wrong number, and it is NOT the arithmetic defect this row was written to catch. WHAT IT IS: neither surface states its SCOPE. A worker who sees 9 on the home screen and 6 in their logbook has no way to reconcile them, and the natural reading - that three jobs went missing - is the wrong one. The row asks that the tile match the logbook page's own filter 'run with the page's predicate rather than a guess at it'; run that way the predicates are genuinely different, so the honest verdict is neither a pass nor an arithmetic failure but THIS: the two figures need scope labels ("hive-wide" / "yours") before either can be reconciled with the other. Fix is copy, not computation - and it is Ian's call whether the home tile should be hive-wide at all for a worker persona. CAUGHT BY CHECKING BEFORE CLAIMING: 9-vs-6 looks exactly like a defect, and this arc has already produced one false 'DISAGREE' finding from deliberate role-scoping. The DB query is what separated the two readings. METHOD: the page is walked signed-in at 1280x1600, given 9s to settle, and its rendered innerText is matched against patterns HARVESTED FROM A LIVE RENDER - never invented at the desk. Each check records the exact string it matched (`saw`), so this verdict can be audited without re-running it, and `--selftest` plants a satisfying AND a violating text per check so one that cannot fire is caught before it banks anything. RAILS THAT SHAPED THIS WALK: (1) a qualifier must sit NEAR the figure it qualifies - the trend check first went green on 'calendar days between failures', which is MTBF's basis on another card; (2) `near()` scans EVERY anchor occurrence, because anchoring on the first match failed skillmatrix's real '19 of 25 possible' on the source chip's earlier 'skill badges'; (3) where a page prints a claim in a fixed phrase, match the PHRASE - '114 of 409 ran late' cannot be confused with the '0 of 30' asset count one clause earlier; (4) the check must be the ROW'S oracle, not a weaker cousin - 5 of 18 cells were LEFT OWED rather than banked on half their claim.

subject.name: a stale sensor tile states its age

scenarios.oracle: a sensor tile that has not updated says when it last did, rather than rendering an old number as current

evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK. The nudge read 'A LIVE sensor reading is 3-sigma outside the recent baseline. Inspect.' The query behind it accepts anything with recorded_at >= now() - interval '24 hours', so a reading taken twenty-three hours ago rendered word-for-word identically to one taken a minute ago, both described as live. That is the exact failure this oracle names: an old number presented as current, on a surface whose whole purpose is telling someone to walk to a machine now. Nothing had to be fetched to fix it - the RPC already selects recorded_at and the client already had it on the object, so the freshness was in hand and simply not shown. The detail line now states when the reading was taken ('A sensor reading from 3 hours ago is 3-sigma outside...'), via _timeAgo, which delegates to the canonical whFmtAgo in utils.js rather than hand-rolling a second relative-time format. When recorded_at is absent the copy falls back to naming the window the query actually guarantees - 'within the last 24 hours' - which is weaker but still true, instead of reverting to the word 'live'.
evidence.checked: Read the RPC's own predicate rather than trusting the word on screen, which is what showed 'live' to be a claim the query cannot support: the 24-hour bound is the guarantee, and it is a wide one. Confirmed recorded_at is in the selected column list before writing copy that depends on it, so the new string cannot render 'from undefined'. Used the existing canonical formatter (whFmtAgo, confirmed present in utils.js and already reached through this page's _timeAgo wrapper) rather than adding a second time format to the page. HONEST LIMIT: this could not be observed rendering. There are currently ZERO anomaly readings inside the 24-hour window, so the nudge does not appear at all right now; the fix is verified structurally and by parse, not by a live sighting, and that is recorded rather than implied.
evidence.value_checked: RPC sensor block: SELECT asset_id, parameter, quality_flag, recorded_at, is_anomaly ... WHERE is_anomaly AND recorded_at >= now() - interval '24 hours' ORDER BY recorded_at DESC LIMIT 1 | before: 'A live sensor reading is 3-sigma...' | after: 'A sensor reading from <age> is 3-sigma...', fallback names the 24-hour window | formatter: _timeAgo -> whFmtAgo (utils.js) | anomaly readings in window right now: 0 (nudge not currently rendered) | index.html: 10 JS blocks all parse

subject.name: the early-access form promises only capture

scenarios.oracle: an email captured is an email, not an account, and the copy does not imply access the product will not grant

evidence.asserts: FIXED THIS WALK, and the page was half-right already. What the form DOES is one insert into early_access_emails - an email, a role, nothing else. No auth user, no hive membership, no access. The confirmation state was honest about that: the button becomes "You're on the list!", which names a list rather than an account. Everything BEFORE the click pulled the other way. The section heads 'Join the hive.', the submit button reads 'Join the Hive', and the microcopy under it opened with 'Free to join', so three elements said join and none said what joining meant. The honest confirmation only arrives AFTER the person has handed over their work email, which is the wrong side of the decision - this oracle is about what the copy promises at the moment of the act. The microcopy now leads with what the form does: 'Adds you to the early-access list, not an account yet - Philippines-first - No spam, ever'. The CTA keeps its energy and the reassurances stay; what changed is that the mechanism is stated before submission rather than revealed after it.
evidence.checked: Traced the write before judging the copy, because 'Join the Hive' would be perfectly honest if the form created a membership: _supabaseSignup inserts into early_access_emails and does nothing else, and 23505 (duplicate) is swallowed as success, so a second submission by the same person is also just a list entry. Read the post-submit branch too rather than stopping at the button label - that is what showed the page already tells the truth, one step too late, and turned this from 'the page lies' into 'the page tells you afterwards'. Left the heading and CTA alone deliberately: the oracle asks that the copy not imply access, not that the marketing be dismantled, and the clarification sits in the line a reader is already given for exactly this purpose.

(honest) | before: heading 'Join the hive.', CTA 'Join the Hive', microcopy 'Free to join - Philippines-first - No spam, ever' | after: 'Adds you to the early-access list, not an account yet - Philippines-first - No spam, ever' | index.html: 10 JS blocks all parse

findings.title: OWED with a precise diagnosis rather than banked or hastily fixed. The anon landing reports tapTargetsUnder44 = 2, and both are `a.inline-flex.items-center` text links: 'See all 45 guides' at 153x24 and 'Read the complete platform...' at 248x20. Wide enough, but 20-24px tall against Ian's 44px glove

FAILS: 2 of 36 effective tap targets inside #mkt-wrap are under the platform's own 44px floor - a.inline-flex items-center gap 266.5x20 via own box; a.inline-flex items-center gap 160.9x24 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER THAT PASSED 750 of 750 AT PAGE LEVEL: the rule is ported verbat
findings.detail: FAILS: 2 of 36 effective tap targets inside #mkt-wrap are under the platform's own 44px floor - a.inline-flex items-center gap 266.5x20 via own box; a.inline-flex items-center gap 160.9x24 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER THAT PASSED 750 of 750 AT PAGE LEVEL: the rule is ported verbatim from the V1 prover, so these are controls the platform's own standard would reject, in a view V1 never opened.  HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why these rows sat owed for so long: CJ was measured platform-wide at V1 and banked there, and V2/V3 stayed owed for ONE reason - nobody could open those views. Resolving all 15 dialog open paths (each read from SOURCE, never matched by label) removed that blocker, and the same measurements now run inside the OPENED dialog. The open-path table lives in tools/dialog_targets.mjs, shared with the modal-exit prover so the two cannot drift apart. SCOPED TO THE DIALOG, NOT THE PAGE, which is the whole point: a dialog OVERLAYS the page, so measuring document.body with a sheet open would re-measure V1 and bank it as V2 - the one-reading-for-every-layer error this bank has already paid for once. Every measurement is rooted at the dialog element. Overflow compares each visible descendant's right edge against the dialog's own content box, with a 1px tolerance (an earlier arc counted a 0.109px abutment as occlusion) and honours overflow-x auto/scroll/hidden/clip on an ancestor INSIDE the dialog, because a deliberately scrollable panel is not a defect. THE TAP-TARGET RULE IS PORTED VERBATIM FROM THE V1 PROVER, NOT REINVENTED, and that correction is why this number means anything. The first cut omitted four of V1's exclusions - sr-only, disabled, the actionable check, and the WCAG 2.5.5 inline-link-in-prose exception - and REPLACED a control's rect with its label instead of UNIONING them. Applying a stricter standard at V2 than at V1 does not find defects, it manufactures a difference between the two views and calls it one. With V1's exact rule restored the count came back IDENTICAL, which is what makes these findings real rather than an artifact: they are measured on the same ruler that banked 750/750 at page level. SCOPE: overflow is measured at THREE widths - 390, 641 and 1280 - and each width's row is banked from its OWN reading, never spread from one width to the others. The dialog is not closed between widths; two animation frames are awaited after each resize so the panel has actually reflowed, and a zero width at ANY width fails the whole target rather than quietly trusting the rest. TAP TARGETS are measured at 390 only - that is the mobile-first floor the V1 prover used, and a control that clears 44px at 390 does not shrink as the viewport grows. Two of the 15 dialogs are UNGRADED with their reason recorded rather than counted: resume's #review-sheet has no read-only path in (it needs the upload -> resume-extract pipeline, which WRITES) and hive's #handover-sheet cannot be reached at all. The walk is NON-WRITING - it opens a dialog, measures, and presses Escape.

Same reasoning as the disabled row:
WITHDRAWN TO OWED, not recorded as a defect: '.oh-tile-num' grew but no wait state was found inside it or in any enclosing region.
findings.detail: WITHDRAWN TO OWED, not recorded as a defect: '.oh-tile-num' grew but no wait state was found inside it or in any enclosing region. That was true of seven other components until an initial-sweep bug in my recorder was fixed, so an absence of evidence here is not yet evidence of absence - it needs a direct poll before it can be called a defect. RE-MEASURED under a CORRECTED recorder, and re-earned rather than re-baselined. The previous reading came from a MutationObserver that armed and then only reported FUTURE mutations - it never swept what was ALREADY in the tree. Arming is also not always at document_start: when document.documentElement is not yet present the recorder falls back to readystatechange, which first fires at 'interactive'. So any wait state painted before that moment was invisible, and an observer with no initial sweep cannot tell 'nothing happened' from 'it happened before I looked'. Measured cost of that blind spot: project-report read as having NO loading state on all three components while a poller saw four; with the sweep added its #exec-summary shows 4 skeletons plus aria-busy at 309ms, at depth 0. Across 22 pages the fix moved 7 components out of FAIL. Same shape as arming at 'interactive' and losing the first 650ms.

findings.title: WITHDRAWN, not recorded as a defect.
findings.detail: WITHDRAWN, not recorded as a defect. This row was banked green asserting the component is STATIC, and a corrected recorder shows it GROWS - so the claim its evidence rested on is false and the row must return to owed rather than keep a verdict nobody can support. The previous reading came from a MutationObserver that reported only FUTURE mutations and never swept what was already in the tree; adding that sweep moved seven components out of FAIL across 22 pages. '.oh-tile-num' grows and the page DOES paint a skeleton at +246ms - but that skeleton sits in #oh-jobs, the open-jobs LIST, and only shares the far ancestor #ops-home (depth 4) with the KPI tiles. So the tiles themselves have no placeholder of their own: the evidence belongs to a different component. Left owed rather than credited, because borrowing a sibling's placeholder is how a component gets a pass for a wait state the person never saw where they were looking.

observed.disposition: owed, evidence belongs to another component

scenarios.question: contrast, focus, motion and naming - the facts a screenshot cannot confirm and a measurement can
scenarios.oracle: an icon-only control has an accessible name that says what it DOES

findings.title: 14 of 21 icon-only controls have NO accessible name (of 52 visible controls)
findings.detail: MEASURED IN A 22-PAGE LIVE-MCP SWEEP at a verified innerWidth of 390. A control counts as icon-only when its VISIBLE text is empty or purely a colour-emoji glyph (\p{Emoji_Presentation}, or a pictograph forced to emoji by VS16, with no letter or number) - the same narrowed test the contrast lens now uses, because the older \p{Extended_Pictographic} check also matched geometric glyphs that are real text. A control counts as NAMED when it carries aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or an sr-only child, read from the accessibility surface a screen reader would actually use rather than inferred from the markup. 14 of 21 icon-only controls carry NO accessible name - no aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or sr-only child. The named ones prove the pattern is known here ('WorkHive home', 'Open menu'), so this is omission, not ignorance. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COUNT: an icon-only control with no name is announced as 'button' - a screen reader user is told something is actionable and not what it does, which is worse than the control being absent, because it invites a blind press. And it is invisible to a sighted-user review, since the icon looks self-explanatory to someone who can see it. STATED HONESTLY: this row is OWED, not failed-and-fixed. The fix is one aria-label per control and it is mechanical, but naming a control is a copy decision (what does this button DO, in the user's words) and there are 14 of them on this page, so it is a real unit of work rather than a find-and-replace. TO CLOSE: enumerate the 14 unnamed controls, give each an aria-label describing its ACTION not its icon, and re-run this probe expecting unnamed 0 of 21.
findings.observed: ctrls 52 / icon-only 21 / unnamed 14, measured live at innerWidth 390

findings.title: RETRACTED - the 'unnamed icon-only controls' finding on this page is a PROBE ARTEFACT: every flagged control has visible text in its innerHTML while my probe read innerText as empty
findings.detail: I recorded this page as having icon-only controls with no accessible name - 14 of 21 on index, 10 of 12 on hive - and framed it as a screen-reader dead end. The evidence contradicts it. DUMPING innerHTML FOR EVERY FLAGGED CONTROL shows real visible labels on all of them. On hive: #stair-explain-btn contains 'Why?', eight anchors contain 'View in PM Scheduler ->', and a button contains 'Load More'. On index: 'Dismiss x', 'All assets ->', and icon+label pairs of the shape ` Logbook` - which is the CORRECT pattern, an aria-hidden icon beside a real text label. None of these is icon-only, and none needs an aria-label; several would be actively worsened by one, since an aria-label overrides the visible text a sighted user reads. THE BUG IS MY DETECTOR: it classified a control as icon-only when `innerText` was empty, and innerText returned '' for these elements even though they passed display/visibility/height checks and their innerHTML plainly holds text. innerText reports RENDERED text and is sensitive to layout state in ways innerHTML is not, so using it as the sole test for 'has a visible label' produced a false positive on every one. The correct test compares the accessible name against text content read a way that does not depend on render state - textContent, or the computed accessible name itself. WHY THIS ONE IS THE WORST OF THE SESSION'S FALSE FINDINGS: it would have sent someone to write 24 aria-labels onto controls that already have correct labels, and aria-label REPLACES the accessible name rather than supplementing it - so 'fixing' it would have DEGRADED accessibility on two pages while reporting an improvement. It is the same family as the labelled-tap-target error earlier today (seven fabricated defects from measuring an input's box instead of its label), and the same root: I tested a convenient property instead of the property the oracle is actually about. TO CLOSE: rebuild the icon-only test on textContent plus the computed accessible name, self-test it with a discriminating pair - a genuinely bare must be REPORTED, and an icon-plus-label button must be SKIPPED - and only then re-read these pages. Until that exists, this row's icon_only_name status is UNKNOWN, not failing.
findings.observed: flagged controls with visible text in innerHTML: hive #stair-explain-btn 'Why?', 8x 'View in PM Scheduler ->', 'Load More'; index 'Dismiss x', 'All assets ->', and .oh-qa-btn icon+label spans. innerText read '' for all of them despite passing display/visibility/height filters.

scenarios.oracle: a person can state what the number means from the surface alone

findings.title: 5 of 9 rendered numbers carry NO adjacent explanation - a bare figure on a maintenance surface is a riddle, not a reading
findings.detail: comprehension() enumerated 9 numerals a person actually reads on this view and found 5 with nothing beside them naming what they are - no label, no unit, no denominator, no period. On hive the unexplained set includes '62' and '100', which is the shape that matters most: a readiness-style score with no visible basis. This platform already has a standing rule that a metric's LABEL is a claim and that a composite nobody can decompose is a vibe with a number attached - these rows are that rule unmet. NOT BANKED, and the row stays owed: the fix comes first, the row is earned after. ONE CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, because this oracle can be satisfied dishonestly: the fix is to state what the number IS and what it is OVER - its denominator, window and unit - not to bolt a generic caption next to it. A label that says 'Score' explains nothing and would still clear the check. Verify against the source view that the stated basis is the ACTUAL basis.

findings.title: LEFT OWED with a diagnosis rather than graded on the wrong path.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED with a diagnosis rather than graded on the wrong path. The walk could only reach the REJECTED branch ('Wrong username or password.'), because a truthful success needs a real auth session and synthesizing one would mean forging a credential - which this bank will not do to make a row green. Graded as-is the row scored PARTIAL, and that verdict would have been about the refusal path while the row's own claim is about the SUCCESS path: a rejection naming no 'next step' is correct behaviour, since the next step after wrong credentials is simply to try again, and inventing a promise there would be worse copy. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS: a genuine signed-out sign-in with real test credentials, which also exercises the opener this walk had to bypass (openSignIn toggles the user menu when a name is stored). The three sibling rows on this view - refusal, double-press and outcome-shown - are banked from the paths that WERE honestly reachable. REACHED BY REVEALING #signin-modal DIRECTLY, and that is a stated compromise rather than a hidden one: openSignIn() checks for a stored worker name first and toggles the USER MENU instead when one exists, so on the signed-in context these provers establish, the page's real opener never reaches this dialog. What is graded here is the dialog's own behaviour, which is identical code either way. It does NOT prove the opener works for a signed-out visitor - that is a different claim and is not made here.

observed.unreachable_branch: successful sign-in (needs a real session, not a forged one)
observed.needed_next: signed-out context with real test credentials

evidence.asserts: after a successful sign-in, the surface makes clear what changed and when
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK ON THE REAL PATH, and this row was deliberately left owed one pass earlier rather than graded on the wrong branch. It is now measured SIGNED OUT, through the page's OWN opener (button.signin-btn -> openSignIn), with real test credentials and a real POST to the login proxy - no synthetic session, because forging a credential to make a row green is not evidence. MEASURED: anon load shows #ops-home at display:none and the modal hidden; pressing the real Sign In control opens the dialog; submitting shows 'Signing in...' with the control disabled; and by +800ms the dialog had CLOSED and #ops-home had become display:block. THE AFTERMATH IS THE DESTINATION ITSELF. This view answers 'what happens next' not with a sentence but by DELIVERING the change immediately - the marketing landing is replaced by the signed-in ops home, which is the strongest available answer to 'what did my press do': the person does not need to be told what will happen because it already has, and they are looking at it. The same reasoning the bank already applies to a past-tense effect clause, applied to a surface transformation. Nothing was rewritten on this page. TWO THINGS WORTH THE NEXT WALKER'S TIME. (1) The credential FORMAT matters and is easy to get wrong: #si-username is labelled 'Username', and signing in with the account's EMAIL (leandromarquez@auth.workhiveph.com) was rejected with 'Wrong username or password.' while the bare username (leandromarquez) succeeded. I am deliberately NOT changing that message: a generic refusal that declines to say WHICH half was wrong is the correct posture for an auth surface, since a more specific one confirms whether an account exists. If it is ever softened, the softening belongs on the FORMAT ('that looks like an email - use your username'), which leaks nothing, not on the credential. (2) documentElement did NOT carry .wh-signed-in on this render - the swap happened through JS on the live page, whereas the pre-body class is what a FRESH load uses. Both routes reach the same view, and the CD invariant about the swap being atomic is the row that should hold them to it.

value_checked.aftermath_shape: the destination is delivered, not described
value_checked.message_left_unchanged: a generic auth refusal is correct; it must not confirm account existence

evidence.asserts: a cross surface handoff journey on this page, walked as this persona, does not make a returning person redo setup
evidence.checked: PASSES: "Hive Live Board: Join or create a team. " -> the auth wall at "index" instead of hive, which is correct for an anon persona following a members-only link; no claim is made about hive's own content. PERSONA: this row was walked as "anon visitor" (slot P1), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'anon'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. That distinction was learned by getting it wrong: clearing the hive key made asset-hub answer, entirely correctly, 'Asset Hub needs a hive ... Go to Hive', and the oracle called it a DEAD END for all three personas - including a supervisor who is demonstrably a member of hive 636cf7e8, which is the giveaway that indicted the probe rather than the page. Clearing the worker-name key likewise bounced signed-in people off achievements, report-sender and project-report. The journey under test is a first-time signed-in MEMBER, so membership and identity are as fixed as the session. NON-VACUITY: a journey that cannot be CONSTRUCTED fails - a page that will not load, or a persona that cannot be established, is a finding about the surface or about this harness's knowledge of it, never a quiet pass. This is the discipline the marketplace spec tests/ux-journeys.spec.ts already carries; this prover extends it to the 22 product pages rather than re-deriving it. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - 13 capture surfaces across the roster opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. 13 of 13 pass: zero rows written, zero silent drafts, every cleanup verified. ★ABANDONMENT IS A RELOAD, NOT A CLOSE. An X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what happens when someone takes a call or their phone dies, and no confirm dialog can intercept it. ★THREE SHAPES, judged separately: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST; a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (a restored draft is the GOOD design - judged on the LABEL, never on the restoration); and a QUEUED WRITE draining later. And the MEASURE FOLLOWS THE SHAPE OF THE WRITE: hive's intent capture mutates a row, so that case compares the VALUE before and after rather than counting rows, which a count-delta could never detect. ★EVERY GREEN IS NON-VACUOUS - the fill is proven to have landed first. Three cases failed LOUDLY on the way in rather than passing quietly: logbook on an invented opener (UNGRADED), pm-scheduler on a guessed column name (task_text; it is item_text), resume on a JSONB column needing ::text. A PROBE WHOSE OWN QUERY IS BROKEN MUST NOT REPORT A FINDING, because its 0 rows look exactly like a page that wrote nothing.  FOR THIS PAGE THE CASE RUNS SIGNED OUT, and getting that wrong would not fail loudly - it would measure a DIFFERENT PAGE. index.html is two products behind one URL: an inline script sets html.wh-signed-in before <body> parses and CSS swaps the marketing landing for the ops dashboard, so #joinForm does not exist for a signed-in probe. Two other provers in this arc hit the same trap on this same page. Abandoning the early-access signup writes nothing.

A page that demands setup on the RETURN which it did not demand on the first run is one finding; a page that demands it BOTH times is a different and lesser one, and the two are reported separately rather than flattened. 'Setup demanded' matches the page asking the person to choose or configure before it will show them anything (choose/select your discipline|trade|role|hive|shift, get started, set up your, complete your profile). J4 two_sided_same_object COMPARES TWO CONCURRENT SESSIONS OF THE SAME IDENTITY, and why it is not two ROLES is a finding in itself. The first version compared a worker's rendering against a supervisor's and reported logbook as '3 of 8 shared figures DISAGREE between two members of the same hive' - #total-count 314 vs 516, #open-count 2 vs 6. Every number was correct: the page deliberately scopes the whole view by role, and the giveaway was a THIRD element - #lb-progress read 'JOBS CLOSED' for the worker and 'TEAM JOBS' for the supervisor. Those are answers to different questions that happen to share an element id, so calling them a contradiction would have banked findings alleging the platform disagrees with itself while it was scoping correctly. Matching on the adjacent label did not rescue it either: #total-count is labelled 'entries' on BOTH sides, and only that other element disclosed the scope - itself a real gap, recorded against CM what_is_this_number rather than smuggled in here. So the second side is the SAME identity in a second session, which is what these pages' own anatomy means by two_context ('two workers, one entry'); role scoping is then identical by construction, and any remaining disagreement is genuine - a race, or a stale cache. Figures are keyed by ELEMENT ID plus the page's own LABEL for that figure (aria-label, else the surrounding card text with the value removed). An id present for only one session is SKIPPED, not failed, because that is authorisation working. A comparison over ZERO shared figures is reported as NOT MEASURED and FAILS - zero disagreements over zero comparisons is not a pass. J5 abandon_resume TYPES INTO A COMPOSER AND WALKS AWAY - the most ordinary thing a person on a plant floor does, because they get called away mid-entry. A marker string is typed into the first visible text field of the page's own dialog (opened via tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the SAME grounded table four other provers read, so this cannot drift from how those views are known to open), the walker then leaves the page entirely and returns. THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES IT FAIR: a preserved DRAFT is good UX, not a defect, so the marker is looked for in two places that mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD = a draft was kept, which PASSES and is noted as deliberate. Out in the page's own CONTENT = it HALF-LANDED, and a person who typed and walked away now holds a record they never submitted. NOTHING IS EVER SUBMITTED, so this stays non-writing: the marker only ever reaches an input's value. COVERAGE IS HONEST: 16 drivable composers exist across 11 of the 22 pages. A page with no composer is left OWED, never failed - 'this surface has nothing to abandon' is a design fact about a read-only page, and manufacturing a red for it is the vacuity R10 exists to forbid. J3 cross_surface_handoff FOLLOWS A REAL LINK OUT, and its claim is deliberately NARROW because a wide one would be dishonest: most in-app links carry no parameter, so there is no 'context' to survive, and asserting that there is would be inventing a property in order to measure it. What is actually checked: (1) the handoff LANDS WHERE THE LINK PROMISED - the href's page is the page reached, so a link that silently bounces elsewhere via an auth wall or redirect has broken the handoff even though it appeared to work; (2) the destination is NOT A DEAD END, on the same rule and the same reasoned-empty exemption J1 uses, so handing off into a well-explained empty state passes and handing off into a blank does not; and (3) IF the link carries a query parameter, the destination must REFLECT it rather than drop it - the only case where 'context survived' is a real checkable claim, and it is checked. A page with no visible in-app link to another product page is left OWED, never failed. SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this row claims exactly ONE of J1 first_run_to_value, J2 repeat_visit or J4 two_sided_same_object, J5 abandon_resume or J3 cross_surface_handoff - one row, one claim, and the others are NOT settled by it. J4 compares two sessions of ONE identity, so it neither claims nor tests cross-ROLE agreement: a supervisor and a worker legitimately see differently scoped figures here. The failed-read tooth above is ARMED but not INDUCED here: this walk exercises a HEALTHY system, so a page passing J1 has not been shown to survive a refused read - inducing that is the CC failure-injection family's job, and a page can pass here and still fail there. NON-WRITING: nothing is typed or submitted; storage is cleared only inside a throwaway context that is closed after each persona.

THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - 13 capture surfaces across the roster opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. 13 of 13 pass: zero rows written, zero silent drafts, every cleanup verified. ★ABANDONMENT IS A RELOAD, NOT A CLOSE. An X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what happens when someone takes a call or their phone dies, and no confirm dialog can intercept it. ★THREE SHAPES, judged separately: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST; a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (a restored draft is the GOOD design - judged on the LABEL, never on the restoration); and a QUEUED WRITE draining later. And the MEASURE FOLLOWS THE SHAPE OF THE WRITE: hive's intent capture mutates a row, so that case compares the VALUE before and after rather than counting rows, which a count-delta could never detect. ★EVERY GREEN IS NON-VACUOUS - the fill is proven to have landed first. Three cases failed LOUDLY on the way in rather than passing quietly: logbook on an invented opener (UNGRADED), pm-scheduler on a guessed column name (task_text; it is item_text), resume on a JSONB column needing ::text. findings.detail: FAILS: UNEXPLAINED — still renders 2 of 5 number(s) non-zero (0 of them also present signed-in, which may be static furniture: none) and nothing on screen says the data could not be loaded. With a session this view rendered 7 non-zero value(s) over 1110 characters; with the auth token removed from storage it rendered 2 over 971, and the page did not redirect, did not add a sign-in prompt it was not already showing, and did not state that anything failed to load. What is on screen after the kill: "Skip to main content Leandro Good morning, Leandro 👋 Thursday, Aug 13 · Morning Shift AI companion Companion: Zaniah 🐝 Baguio Textile Mills EN FIL Sign Out ✓ ALL CLEAR No".  WHY THIS FINDING IS WORDED NARROWLY, and what it deliberately does NOT claim: the obvious reading - 'the page should have redirected or announced an ended session' - is WRONG on this platform, and checking that is what kept this row honest. index.html:3520 shows a designed branch for 'Guest worker (has name, no auth session)' which shows an upgrade nudge, and index.html:902-906 stamps its wh-signed-in paint-hint from wh_last_worker + wh_active_hive_id in localStorage precisely so a known user does not watch the marketing landing collapse into the dashboard (a measured CLS of 0.24). So a cached identity with no session is a SUPPORTED state here, not a defect, and demanding a redirect would have manufactured one. What is not defensible is the other half: hive-scoped reads that could not have succeeded rendering as zeros with nothing saying so. On index that surfaces as the words 'ALL CLEAR - Nothing urgent right now' beside the real hive name - an affirmative safety claim derived from a read that never happened, which is the same shape as the two moderation badges that asserted '0 waiting' on a failed read. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, live, and what the oracle deliberately is NOT: it is not 'does the page redirect to sign-in'. Several of these surfaces are legitimately readable signed-out, so a redirect is only ONE honest answer and demanding it would manufacture defects on the public pages. The oracle is the NEGATIVE: a page must never present a signed-out state as though it were signed-in data. Three behaviours are accepted and the row NAMES which one this page did - (1) redirect to a sign-in surface or render a sign-in prompt it was not rendering before, (2) render an empty state that STATES its reason, (3) be a genuinely public surface that renders identical content either way. What FAILS is the fourth: hive-scoped numbers still on screen, or bare zeros and dashes with no explanation, standing in for a read that could not have succeeded. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT IN COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in and the probe would measure nothing while reporting a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH localStorage and sessionStorage is swept (hardcoding one project ref is the other way this goes silently vacuous), then the page is RELOADED so the client re-reads storage from cold. THE CONTROL IS THE SIGNED-IN READING, TAKEN FIRST: the same page is measured with a session, and the two readings must differ. A probe that cannot prove it changed anything cannot report that the change was handled correctly - so a page that looks identical either way is either genuinely public (case 3, and then it must show no hive-scoped values at all) or the kill did not take, and those two are never allowed to be confused: the second is recorded UNGRADED, never as a pass. TWO FALSE READINGS WERE CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, and both are why this row is trustworthy. FIRST, THE PROVER REPORTED A PASS OVER AN EMPTY DENOMINATOR: the text-matching regexes were declared in Node scope but referenced inside the page.evaluate callback, which runs in the BROWSER, so every page threw ReferenceError and came back UNGRADED - and the summary printed 'PASS - no page presents a dead session as signed-in data', true only in the sense that no page had been looked at. Zero failures over zero measurements is now an explicit FAIL, louder than a real failure, because a failure gets triaged while a vacuous green gets banked. SECOND, A BODY-WIDE KEYWORD MATCH READ THE PAGE'S OWN MARKETING COPY AS EVIDENCE: public-feed was credited with 'says-signed-out' because its text matched /sign in/ - but it matched BEFORE the kill too, since the page permanently renders 'Sign In ->' and 'Sign in to join the conversation' as its read-only CTA, and its body was byte-identical either way at 2438 characters with zero non-zero values both times. A signed-out sentence now only counts if it APPEARED after the kill, and the unchanged/public case is tested BEFORE any text match rather than after it - which is how public-feed came to be recorded as what it actually is, a public surface, rather than as a page that announced a dead session. THIRD, A LEAK SUB-CHECK WAS BUILT AND THEN DELIBERATELY DEMOTED TO INFORMATIONAL, because it could not tell leaked USER data from static FURNITURE and it got that wrong in BOTH directions. Comparing the signed-in and signed-out readings for values that survived, it called index a leak on a bare '3' with no class - a coincidence between a step indicator and a tile - and then, after being tightened to require a class and more than one digit, it called achievements a leak on 18/38/63/83 .wh-avatar-lvl, which are the Iron/Bronze/Silver/Gold tier THRESHOLDS: identical for every user and CORRECT to survive a signed-out reload. Telling those apart requires knowing which numbers are user-scoped, which no generic DOM read can answer, so claiming it anyway would be manufacturing findings. The oracle now grades ONLY the classification it can actually establish, and the survivor list travels with the row as context for a human rather than as a verdict. FOURTH, THE FAILING VERDICT MISDESCRIBED ITS OWN MEASUREMENT: it read 'N number(s), all zero/blank' on every page that reached that branch, while achievements had 6 of 9 non-zero. A verdict that contradicts its own reading is the mislabelled-metric defect wearing a test's clothes; it now states the counts it measured. FIFTH, A PAGE STILL LOADING WAS BEING REPORTED AS A PAGE THAT FAILED TO EXPLAIN ITSELF. The sweep called asset-hub, analytics and shift-brain UNEXPLAINED EMPTY with ZERO numbers on screen - but zero numbers is equally the signature of a page that had not finished rendering 3.4 seconds after a reload, which is the SLOW-vs-STUCK distinction the component-states prover already had to learn. A page that looks under-rendered, or is still showing aria-busy / skeleton / spinner elements, now gets another 6 seconds and is re-read; if it is still unsettled the row is UNGRADED rather than failed, because the reading genuinely cannot tell the two apart. SIXTH, THE ORACLE WAS FAILING PAGES THAT HAVE NO SUBJECT. assistant and report-sender rendered ZERO non-zero values even WITH a session - a chat thread and an empty report list - so there is no figure on either page that a dead session could turn into a false reassurance. Failing them would be asserting a defect in the absence of the thing the assertion is about, so a page with no data signed-in is now UNGRADED with that reason recorded. Across six corrections the pattern is the same one this whole bank keeps teaching: the instrument was wrong more often than the pages were, and every one of these was caught by reading what the page actually rendered instead of trusting the verdict. SEVENTH, THE READINESS GUARD ITSELF WAS TOO BLUNT AND DISQUALIFIED FINISHED PAGES. Counting elements matching skeleton/spinner/aria-busy selectors by SELECTOR ALONE flipped public-feed from a correct pass to UNGRADED on 1 busy element at 2473 rendered characters, and did the same to engineering-design (3 at 1851) and report-sender (2 at 1176) - because pages routinely leave a skeleton node in the DOM with display:none once the real content arrives. A hidden skeleton is a template, not a loading state, so only VISIBLE busy elements count. EIGHTH, A PASSING VERDICT NAMED A MECHANISM IT HAD NOT ESTABLISHED: an unchanged page with no figures was labelled 'public-surface-identical-signed-out' and PASSED, which called project-report - a hive report page - a public surface purely because it renders no numbers in either state. Every PASS must now rest on POSITIVE evidence (a redirect, a prompt that appeared, a sentence that appeared, a stated reason for being empty); an unchanged reading and a view with no figures at all are both UNGRADED, with the reason recorded, so they stay owed rather than being banked on a label nobody proved. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: this is V1, the page as it loads, and it settles the CLIENT's behaviour when the stored session is gone. It does not test an EXPIRED-but-present token (a different path: the server refuses and the client must translate that refusal), nor a session that dies mid-action while a write is in flight. Those are separate oracles and stay owed rather than inheriting this reading. The walk is NON-WRITING - it reads, clears client-side storage in its own browser context, and reloads - so it cannot have touched the shared test database.
