findings.detail: FAILS: UNEXPLAINED — still renders 2 of 5 number(s) non-zero (0 of them also present signed-in, which may be static furniture: none) and nothing on screen says the data could not be loaded. With a session this view rendered 4 non-zero value(s) over 569 characters; with the auth token removed from storage it rendered 2 over 444, and the page did not redirect, did not add a sign-in prompt it was not already showing, and did not state that anything failed to load. What is on screen after the kill: "Skip to main content Leandro Good evening, Leandro 👋 Thursday, Aug 13 · Evening Shift AI companion Companion: Zaniah 🐝 Baguio Textile Mills EN FIL Sign Out ✓ ALL CLEAR No".  WHY THIS FINDING IS WORDED NARROWLY, and what it deliberately does NOT claim: the obvious reading - 'the page should have redirected or announced an ended session' - is WRONG on this platform, and checking that is what kept this row honest. index.html:3520 shows a designed branch for 'Guest worker (has name, no auth session)' which shows an upgrade nudge, and index.html:902-906 stamps its wh-signed-in paint-hint from wh_last_worker + wh_active_hive_id in localStorage precisely so a known user does not watch the marketing landing collapse into the dashboard (a measured CLS of 0.24). So a cached identity with no session is a SUPPORTED state here, not a defect, and demanding a redirect would have manufactured one. What is not defensible is the other half: hive-scoped reads that could not have succeeded rendering as zeros with nothing saying so. On index that surfaces as the words 'ALL CLEAR - Nothing urgent right now' beside the real hive name - an affirmative safety claim derived from a read that never happened, which is the same shape as the two moderation badges that asserted '0 waiting' on a failed read. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, live, and what the oracle deliberately is NOT: it is not 'does the page redirect to sign-in'. Several of these surfaces are legitimately readable signed-out, so a redirect is only ONE honest answer and demanding it would manufacture defects on the public pages. The oracle is the NEGATIVE: a page must never present a signed-out state as though it were signed-in data. Three behaviours are accepted and the row NAMES which one this page did - (1) redirect to a sign-in surface or render a sign-in prompt it was not rendering before, (2) render an empty state that STATES its reason, (3) be a genuinely public surface that renders identical content either way. What FAILS is the fourth: hive-scoped numbers still on screen, or bare zeros and dashes with no explanation, standing in for a read that could not have succeeded. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT IN COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in and the probe would measure nothing while reporting a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH localStorage and sessionStorage is swept (hardcoding one project ref is the other way this goes silently vacuous), then the page is RELOADED so the client re-reads storage from cold. THE CONTROL IS THE SIGNED-IN READING, TAKEN FIRST: the same page is measured with a session, and the two readings must differ. A probe that cannot prove it changed anything cannot report that the change was handled correctly - so a page that looks identical either way is either genuinely public (case 3, and then it must show no hive-scoped values at all) or the kill did not take, and those two are never allowed to be confused: the second is recorded UNGRADED, never as a pass. TWO FALSE READINGS WERE CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BANKED, and both are why this row is trustworthy. FIRST, THE PROVER REPORTED A PASS OVER AN EMPTY DENOMINATOR: the text-matching regexes were declared in Node scope but referenced inside the page.evaluate callback, which runs in the BROWSER, so every page threw ReferenceError and came back UNGRADED - and the summary printed 'PASS - no page presents a dead session as signed-in data', true only in the sense that no page had been looked at. Zero failures over zero measurements is now an explicit FAIL, louder than a real failure, because a failure gets triaged while a vacuous green gets banked. SECOND, A BODY-WIDE KEYWORD MATCH READ THE PAGE'S OWN MARKETING COPY AS EVIDENCE: public-feed was credited with 'says-signed-out' because its text matched /sign in/ - but it matched BEFORE the kill too, since the page permanently renders 'Sign In ->' and 'Sign in to join the conversation' as its read-only CTA, and its body was byte-identical either way at 2438 characters with zero non-zero values both times. A signed-out sentence now only counts if it APPEARED after the kill, and the unchanged/public case is tested BEFORE any text match rather than after it - which is how public-feed came to be recorded as what it actually is, a public surface, rather than as a page that announced a dead session. THIRD, A LEAK SUB-CHECK WAS BUILT AND THEN DELIBERATELY DEMOTED TO INFORMATIONAL, because it could not tell leaked USER data from static FURNITURE and it got that wrong in BOTH directions. Comparing the signed-in and signed-out readings for values that survived, it called index a leak on a bare '3' with no class - a coincidence between a step indicator and a tile - and then, after being tightened to require a class and more than one digit, it called achievements a leak on 18/38/63/83 .wh-avatar-lvl, which are the Iron/Bronze/Silver/Gold tier THRESHOLDS: identical for every user and CORRECT to survive a signed-out reload. Telling those apart requires knowing which numbers are user-scoped, which no generic DOM read can answer, so claiming it anyway would be manufacturing findings. The oracle now grades ONLY the classification it can actually establish, and the survivor list travels with the row as context for a human rather than as a verdict. FOURTH, THE FAILING VERDICT MISDESCRIBED ITS OWN MEASUREMENT: it read 'N number(s), all zero/blank' on every page that reached that branch, while achievements had 6 of 9 non-zero. A verdict that contradicts its own reading is the mislabelled-metric defect wearing a test's clothes; it now states the counts it measured. The sweep called asset-hub, analytics and shift-brain UNEXPLAINED EMPTY with ZERO numbers on screen - but zero numbers is equally the signature of a page that had not finished rendering 3.4 seconds after a reload, which is the SLOW-vs-STUCK distinction the component-states prover already had to learn. evidence.asserts: a second press cannot register the same address twice
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with the insert HELD, so the in-flight window is real. Pressed 'Join the Hive' twice: the second press was BLOCKED - the control is disabled during flight - and the write count stayed at ONE. On a FAILED insert the second press does write again, which is right: that is a retry of something that never happened. Worth noting the write itself is also idempotent by design - the handler swallows Postgres 23505 (unique violation), so a duplicate address cannot create a duplicate row even if a press escaped the guard. ONE INSTRUMENT NOTE, because it nearly cost a verdict: the button's LABEL CHANGES during flight, so a text-based finder loses it exactly when the in-flight double press needs measuring - my first run reported 'no join button' for the second press, which is indistinguishable from 'the press was blocked'. Addressing the control by a stamped data attribute instead settled it: the second press is genuinely BLOCKED because the button is disabled. THE FORM IS WELL BUILT AND THE MEASUREMENTS SAY SO PRECISELY. #join-email carries the HTML required attribute, so an empty submit is refused by NATIVE constraint validation before any network call - validationMessage 'Please fill out this field.', ZERO writes. In flight the control reads 'Joining...' and is disabled, and #join-email is disabled with it. On success the control becomes "You're on the list!" and STAYS disabled. On failure it reverts to 'Try again' and re-enables the email, the role select and itself. MEASURED IN THREE MODES with the early_access_emails insert held, answered 201, and answered 500. WALKED SIGNED OUT, which this view requires and nothing else in this session has needed: V2 only exists for an anonymous visitor. Confirmed on load - #mkt-wrap visible, #ops-home at display:none - so the reading is of the landing and not of the dashboard behind the same URL. That two-products-one-URL split is the defining fact about this page.

value_checked.belt_and_braces: handler ignores 23505, so a duplicate address cannot duplicate a row

Pressed Sign In twice 120ms apart: ONE request, the second press fired nothing, and the surface showed it - submitSignIn sets the control to 'Signing in...' and disables it before dispatching. That guard matters more here than on most controls: sign-in is routed through a server-side brute-force-protected login proxy that gates by real attempt count, so a double-tap would spend two of a person's own attempts on one intent. What is graded here is the dialog's own behaviour, which is identical code either way. It does NOT prove the opener works for a signed-out visitor - that is a different claim and is not made here.
